name: Field Doctor-Style Chicken Korma (Low FODMAP)
ingredients:
760 g Chicken
560 g Whole grain rice
3 1/2 medium Sweet Potatoes
235 g Broccoli
205 g Soy Milk [SOY beans, water]
205 g Spinach
1 1/4 medium Courgettes
55 g Coconut Milk [Coconut, Water]
48 g Ginger
2/3 Lemon Juice
1 1/4 tbsp Brown Sugar
1 1/2 tbsp Sweet Noble Paprika
1 1/2 tbsp Coriander
1 1/2 tsp Turmeric Blend
1/2 tsp Sea Salt
2/3 tsp Tapioca Starch
1/4 tsp Chicken Stock (Chicken Extract, Chicken Fat, Salt], Garam Masala, Black Pepper
directions:
1. Rice: Cook wholegrain rice until tender; drain and keep warm.

2. Sauce: Warm extra virgin olive oil with ginger. Add turmeric blend, garam masala, sweet paprika and black pepper. Stir in soy milk, coconut milk, lemon juice, brown sugar and chicken stock; simmer gently.

3. Chicken & veg: Brown diced chicken in a little oil, then add to the sauce with sweet potato, broccoli and courgette. Simmer until chicken is cooked and vegetables are tender. Thicken with tapioca slurry if needed. Season with salt.

4. Finish: Fold in spinach until wilted. Serve over rice with coriander.
 
Cool, portion into 8, refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze; reheat until piping hot.
description:
Ingredients: Chicken, Whole grain rice, Sweet Potato, Water, Broccoli, Soy Milk [SOY beans, water], Spinach, Courgette...

Home recreation inspired by Field Doctor Chicken Korma (Low FODMAP) (~405 g ready meal). Scaled to 8 portions. Not an official Field Doctor recipe. https://www.fielddoctor.co.uk/products/aromatic-chicken-curry
notes:
REVERSE-ENGINEERED from Field Doctor published ingredients for personal home cooking only. Official meal is Monash Low FODMAP certified at single-serve size.

Scaling notes
Scaled for 8 portions from Field Doctor single serve (~405 g x 8 = 3240 g).
Unlabelled amounts inferred from UK descending-weight ingredient order (each item <= the one above and >= the one below; leftover mass shared on that basis, not equally).
Spoon measures use ingredient density (g per tsp) then round to kitchen fractions.
Amounts above 50 g are rounded to the nearest 5 g for cooking convenience.
Sweet peppers ~140 g each; carrots ~80 g; sweet potatoes ~130 g; courgettes ~175 g; aubergines ~250 g; swedes ~800 g; plum tomatoes = 400 g tins; lemon ~45 ml / lime ~30 ml juice.
Duplicate label ingredients merged (higher amount kept).
Liquid for home cooking: cook rice, quinoa, pasta, noodles and potatoes in water as you normally would (salt the water; drain where appropriate). For sauces, braises and stir-fry glazes, add water or stock gradually until the consistency is right — do not try to measure the ready-meal's residual water.
Low FODMAP: no onion or garlic bulbs — use chives / green tops only. Inspired recreation from Field Doctor ingredients, not an official recipe.
Chives listed in grams to match fresh packs (e.g. Waitrose Cooks' Ingredients Chives, 20 g).
Ready-meal residual water was ~237 g (inferred ~7.31% from list order) and is not listed as an ingredient.
Oil for home cooking: where Extra Virgin Olive Oil was only a cooking fat on the label, it is omitted from ingredients — fry, soften, sear or roast in extra virgin olive oil as needed. It is kept as an ingredient on richer/oil-forward dishes (e.g. pesto-style sauces or high oil content).
Ready-meal residual Extra Virgin Olive Oil was ~55 g (inferred ~1.70% from list order) and is treated as cooking fat (fry in extra virgin olive oil) rather than a measured ingredient.
